comparison: Both strongly support the core finding of strong perturbation responses across models (C1, C2, C21-C23, C62-C63). OpenEval provides detailed technical validation of computational methods and metrics, while peer reviewers emphasize the novelty and solid evidence for emergent properties. Peer review includes C3, C24, C25 which OpenEval addresses separately.

OpenEval evaluates comparison with toy models (C3, C25, C36) as supported. Peer review R1 includes C3 and C25 in their broader assessment of core findings, affirming the distinction between realistic and toy models without separate detailed analysis.

Perfect claim overlap (C4, C26, C27, C70, C71). Both strongly support findings about adenylate cofactors and specific metabolites driving strong responses. OpenEval emphasizes computational validation and Sobol' sensitivity analysis, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm the discovery of metabolite-specific effects.

High overlap on negative feedback and allosteric regulation (C28-C32). Both support these mechanistic findings. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of control theory basis, while peer reviewers accept the pyruvate and adenylate cofactor findings as adequately addressed. OpenEval includes C33 not mentioned in peer review.

Both support network topology findings (C5, C37-C39). OpenEval emphasizes robustness across reaction addition strategies, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm solid evidence for emergent properties related to network topology and the sparse vs. dense network distinction. Peer review includes broader contextual claims (C34-C35) in R9.

Perfect claim overlap (C40-C42, C59-C60). Both support minimal model findings demonstrating cofactor dynamics drive response behavior. OpenEval provides detailed technical validation, while peer reviewers accept without challenge, implicitly validating through overall positive assessment.

Perfect claim overlap (C13-C18, C43-C45, C66-C67). Both support model descriptions and differences as valid methodological context. OpenEval emphasizes importance for establishing robustness, while peer reviewers accept as part of valuable comparative analysis without challenge.

Perfect claim overlap (C50-C52). Both support model modifications as necessary methodological details. OpenEval notes transparency but raises questions about biological accuracy, while peer reviewers implicitly accept through statement that concerns were adequately addressed.

High overlap on perturbation methodology (C19, C53-C54, C68-C69). Both support the theoretical justification and perturbation strength choices. OpenEval provides detailed quantitative validation, while peer reviewers implicitly accept through lack of critique and positive assessment of systematic perturbation analysis.

Both address nonlinear analysis necessity (C24). OpenEval provides specific computational validation showing linearized models fail, while peer reviewers include this in broader affirmation of core findings without separate detailed discussion.

Partial overlap on background literature claims (C6-C12). OpenEval validates these as appropriately cited context, while peer review R9 groups broader set of literature claims (C6-C12, C34-C36, C47, C55-C58, C72-C73) together, accepting without challenge.

Both address speculative claims about biological implications. OpenEval rates C46-C47 as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of direct evidence for amplification hypothesis. Peer reviewers support broader implications (C46, C48-C49) as valuable future directions, accepting interpretative claims without challenge.

High overlap on practical applications (C48-C49). OpenEval supports these as appropriately cited prior work establishing relevance. Peer reviewers affirm the work provides initiative for future quantitative analysis, accepting broader implications including metabolic engineering applications.

OpenEval evaluates experimental literature on cofactor dynamics (C55-C58, C72-C73) as supported with appropriate citations. Peer review R9 groups these with other background claims, accepting without challenge as valid biological context.

OpenEval provides specific validation of mathematical definition of response coefficient χ (C65). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this technical detail was not separately discussed by reviewers.
